classification.difficultyReason: Convert the line gradient to the perpendicular tangent gradient, solve the resulting derivative equation as a quadratic, and recover both points on the curve.

content.prompt: Find the coordinates of the points on $y=2x^3-2x^2$ where the tangent is perpendicular to the line $2x-y=5$.

answer.worked:
The line $y=2x-5$ has gradient $2$, so the perpendicular tangent has gradient $-\frac12$.

$$\begin{align*}y'&=6x^2-4x\\6x^2-4x&=-\frac12\\12x^2-8x+1&=0\\(6x-1)(2x-1)&=0\\x&=\frac16\quad\text{or}\quad x=\frac12\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}y\big|_{x=\frac16}&=2\left(\frac16\right)^3-2\left(\frac16\right)^2\\y\big|_{x=\frac16}&=-\frac5{108}\\y\big|_{x=\frac12}&=2\left(\frac12\right)^3-2\left(\frac12\right)^2\\y\big|_{x=\frac12}&=-\frac14\end{align*}$$

The points are $\left(\frac16,-\frac5{108}\right)$ and $\left(\frac12,-\frac14\right)$.
